bullets.text: Identity and self-describing information for the HPM and peripherals.

reference_links.label: FRU, Discovery & Boot v0.7 RC1 · pp. 32–34, 132

slides.title: FRU Formats, JSON Locality and Authenticity

synthesis_chunks: Don't confuse a data format with a storage location. I P M I Fru records provide inventory and record structures. D M T F Fru files include descriptors that tell the B M C how to find the associated JSON. The Resident and Context fields help distinguish data in the information device from data elsewhere.

Local JSON contains attributes needed early in discovery. Extended attributes can be obtained through other locations or mechanisms. Both are JSON; local and extended describe their role and availability, not two competing formats.

The specification requires a method for cryptographically verifying Fru information authenticity. When a digital signature is supplied, it must cover all static data in the information device and be stored in a D M T F Fru file.

The hash must be at least SHA three hundred eighty-four, the signature algorithm must be an industry standard, and the algorithm and hash size must be disclosed. Post-quantum signing support is recommended.

bullets.text: Provide basic inventory and the M-PNP-related record structures.
File descriptors identify JSON locations; Resident, Context, Offset and Size guide retrieval.
Required local attributes support early discovery. Extended attributes can be stored or retrieved elsewhere; locality is not a separate data format.
A cryptographic verification method is required. When supplied, a digital signature covers all static FRU contents and is stored as a DMTF FRU file.
Minimum SHA-384 hash; industry-standard signature algorithm; disclose the algorithm and hash size. PQC signing support is recommended.

slides.title: Apply the M-PNP Contract

term_glossary.tooltip: Modular Plug-and-Play; the MHS layer that lets BMC firmware discover and operate conforming hardware from self-describing data.
Data Center Modular Hardware System; OCP's modular server hardware family that M-PNP builds on.
Host Processor Module; the compute module containing the processor complex and platform logic.
Secure Control Module; the management and control module that carries the BMC, root of trust, firmware storage, and platform control functions.
Baseboard Management Controller; the management processor that discovers hardware, reads FRU data, and coordinates platform boot.
Field Replaceable Unit; a replaceable component that exposes identity and descriptive information to platform management firmware.
Legacy FRU information format used for basic component identification and inventory records.
DMTF FRU data format used for richer FRU descriptions, including structures M-PNP can use for signed metadata and file descriptors.
Security Protocol and Data Model; a DMTF protocol used for device authentication, measurement, and attestation flows.
Platform Level Data Model; a DMTF management protocol family used here as one access path for file transfer and platform data exchange.
Modular Peripheral Sideband Tunneling Interface; the sideband tunneling path used for peripheral discovery and control in DC-MHS systems.
LVDS Tunneling Protocol and Interface; a DC-SCM sideband transport for carrying low-pin-count management signals.
Memory-Mapped Buffer Interface; DMTF DSP0282 interface for BMC-to-BIOS communication during early boot.
Field-Programmable Gate Array; one programmable implementation of an applicable M-PNP device role, not the whole v0.7 PD scope.
Control/status register; a memory-mapped register the BMC reads or writes to inspect state or request actions.
A programmable-device function block with defined behaviour, registers and self-description.
Logical sideband signals carried over transports like SGPIO or LTPI instead of dedicated physical pins.
A named power-state checkpoint that holds the applicable hardware before release; required security actions follow the platform security profile.
Universal Backplane Management; a backplane management framework used with NVMe and other storage backplane designs.
Power Distribution Board; a board that distributes platform power and can publish FRU and JSON data.
Programmable Device; the v0.7 scope covers primary HPM and peripheral devices, with FPGA/CPLD and other programmable implementations.
Serial General Purpose Input Output; one of the two permitted required-interface choices for the primary HPM PD.
